prerequisites: Mastery of circuit analysis acquired in 'Circuit Theory' or 'Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering'.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated through the formulation and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to electronic systems, amplifiers, amplifier models and practical applications.
Operational amplifiers, analysis techniques (sum-point restriction), ideal and real operational amplifier models.
Diodes, characteristics, basic circuit applications, basic semiconductor physics, internal diode operation.
Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs), basic operation, essential external characteristics, single-transistor amplifier circuits.
Field Effect Transistors (FETs), basic characteristics, Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor FETs (MOSFETs) of accumulation, analysis and design of biasing circuits for FET amplifiers.
Additional electronic devices, solar cells, silicon controlled rectifier.
teaching_methods: Distance learning technology in virtual classrooms
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 90% from the presential exam, 5% from laboratory practices, and 5% from continuous assessment tests. To pass the course, students must pass both the presential exam and the laboratory practices. The presential exam requires at least three correct answers in the short questions section (out of six) to pass that part and have the rest of the exam graded; a minimum score of 5 out of 10 on the exam is required for the continuous assessment tests to be added to the final grade. Laboratory practices are mandatory and can only be attended after passing the presential exam; failure to attend practices after passing the exam allows for a re-invitation in the extraordinary call, retaining the ordinary exam grade.
